observations: Every vehicle run is preceded by a checkpoint (pier C1/C3, dock C5) and its crates sit on the boost line - high execution, no search.
The two count traps on foot are SUPPORT-ORDER problems (bounce crate before breaking it; ! before the platforms drop).
Nitro are part of the total: the ones the player avoids are paid by the detonator after the boss.
The optional green-gem path holds 22 of 196 crates (11 %) and the bonus 29 (15 %).

geometryObservations: Each jetboard run adds one hazard family. J1 has whirlpools only at the flanks of an 8-12 u lane (O-S2-a). J2 puts mines and whirlpools inside a ~10 u lane, cutting 2-4 u channels (O-S6-a/b); the run's first death came here. J3 adds telegraphed impact rings, cannons and chasers in a 6-8 u channel with a 2-3 u whirlpool gate (G-S9-a), and ends in an arena that reuses the chasers as the boss weapon.

On foot, every hazard first appears alone on plain planks. An anchor hangs on the flank (1:12:28.5), then a spiked roller stands alone (1:12:39.5), then a roller comes with an anchor (1:12:42-47), and then a lone pirate waits on a wide dock (E-S1-a). Only after that do hazards combine.

Water is the only gap type, and on foot it is never crossed by a plain jump longer than about 3 u. Long crossings use devices: rope swings (G-S1-b/c), rafts (P-S4-a, P-G-a), phase platforms (P-S7-b) and the jetboard. Plain jumps stay at 1-3 u (slabs, plank holes, pillars).
The raft rides are side views. Gap widths stay fixed at 1-2 u (G-S4-a), and the raft supplies the challenge: it sets a no-stop beat (J-S4-a), and the camera shows each dock before it arrives.
Vertical clearance is introduced only on the raft. Booms about 1 u above the deck (O-S4-b) are the level's single slide check, and GR ties crates to them (slide-jump under the lower barriers).

The tallest climb is optional. The hidden gem sits on an uncounted 2x3 iron block, 2-3 u above the passing raft (P-S5-b, G-S5-a), so it tests vertical timing from a moving platform without blocking the clear.

The S7 pillar line is the only stepping-stone gauntlet. It stacks two crossing rhythms (anchors O-S7-a, leaping fish O-S7-b) on 2-3 u gaps, and it killed the player once. It starts right after the mask pickup, which also saves (CHECKPOINT text 1:17:22), so a retry is cheap.

Enemy roles escalate. The S1 pirate teaches (E-S1-a) and the raft pirate gates timing (E-S4-a). The launch pirate keeps the gate (E-S5-a), two causeway pirates walk into a TNT as bait (E-S8-a), and in the last run the chasers become tools against mines and against Louise (E-S9-a, E-S10-b).
The vehicle runs telegraph everything that comes from above. Mortar or cannon shots ring the water before they land (O-S9-a), and Louise highlights her slam strip about 2 s ahead (O-S10-a, PS).

Lanes narrow run by run while run length grows: about 11 s for J1, about 20 s for J2 (the clean retry) and about 66 s for J3, before the arena. The checkpoint before each run (CHECKPOINT text 1:13:12, C3, C5) pays for the restart that any jetboard hit causes (GP).

Crates and geometry agree in J1 and S4, where crates float on the safe line or sit on reachable docks. In J2 the mines push the crate line off the safe line, and in S8 a TNT doubles as the trap for the advancing enemies.

Hazards are recycled across modes. The anchor appears on foot (S1), on the raft (G) and over pillars (S7, S8). Cannons fire at the raft (G) and then at the jetboard (S9). Spikes are rollers on foot (S1), logs on the docks (S4) and maces on the raft (S4).
geometryTransfer: Three-run skate lane. Run 1 is 10-14 m wide (9-12 crates) with hazards only at the edges and 8 single crates 1.2-1.6 m above the deck on the centre line. Run 2 is the same width with `pit` discs or mine-like hazards that leave 2.5-4.5 m channels. Run 3 is 7-9 m wide with a hazard pair leaving one 2.5-3.5 m gate. At cruise (12 m/s), runs of about 11, 20 and 66 s, as in Crash, are about 130, 240 and 790 m long. Put a checkpoint before each run.

Raft section as a `mover`. A 5 x 2 m platform travels at walking pace beside a row of 2.3-4.6 m docks set 1.2-2.3 m from its edge. Docks hold crates, one `grunt` and one TNT, and the player hops off and back in under 2 s. Add a boom with its underside 0.6-0.8 m above the mover deck (below the 0.92 m player box) as the slide check, and never a gap wider than one full jump (5.6 m).

Pillar gauntlet. Use 2.3 m square pillars with 2.3-3.5 m gaps over a `pit`, crossed by two `pendulum`s with different periods. Place it right after a checkpoint, since it is the only stepping-stone test of the level.

Chaser-as-tool. On the board, a `charger` that follows the rider and dies on contact with a hazard, together with a mine field where luring it clears both, gives the rider a reason to steer near danger on purpose.

Enemy walks into TNT. On a 3.5 m causeway, two `grunt`s patrol toward the player with a TNT between them. Stomping the TNT (3 s fuse, 2.75 m blast) while they close in teaches the blast radius without risk to the player.
Telegraph everything that falls: ring decals on the deck 1-2 s before an impact (mortar shots, slams), matching the ~2 s warning of Louise.
